note: Per-profile career-project list. One REAL flagship project per real (non-consulting) company, within that company's date range, each chosen because it spans the application, backend/platform, and data/AI layers in a single request path (so the resume can claim all three layers from one coherent project). For the 2 MOST RECENT companies (isRecentTwo:true) we keep company info only - bullets are tailored live at generation. For older companies we ship ready-made bullets, pitched at the seniority appropriate to that point in the career. Consulting companies (consulting:true) store NO project - at generation their engagements are pulled from shared.json (industry-matched entry + 1 more arbitrary). Descriptions are plain-terms, one paragraph.

projects.flagshipProject: FAIR AI Industrialization Platform + RITA Enterprise AI Assistant
projects.description: Foundry for AI by Rackspace (FAIR) is Rackspace's framework for taking enterprise AI ideas from experimentation into secure, production-ready systems, with RITA as one of its flagship internal Generative AI applications. An employee uses RITA to ask IT, security-policy, and operational questions or complete supported self-service workflows; behind the interface, enterprise documents are ingested and indexed, retrieval finds the most relevant authorized content, an LLM produces a grounded response with source references, and evaluation and monitoring check quality before and after release. The broader FAIR industrialization path provides reusable patterns for model and prompt lifecycle management, deployment, evaluation, governance, observability, and scalable AI infrastructure across cloud environments. It touches the backend layer (AI services, APIs, orchestration, and deployment workflows), the data/AI layer (RAG, embeddings, retrieval, evaluation, and model lifecycle), the infrastructure layer (containers, Kubernetes, GPU-backed training and inference, and cloud services), and the security/governance layer (access controls, auditability, data protection, and release gates).

Consulting / client-services company - project summaries are NOT stored here. At generation, the code reads shared.json, picks the entry whose industry matches the JD's extracted client_industry PLUS one more arbitrary project, and uses those as this company's engagements (each opening with a 'did X for a [industry] client' master line).

The production ML platform was the team's path for moving machine-learning work out of notebooks and into repeatable applications. An engineer develops and evaluates NLP or classification models over client text and transactional data; automated training and evaluation workflows compare experiments; approved models are packaged into versioned containerized inference services with rollback support; and experiment tracking records which model and configuration produced each result. It touches the backend layer (inference endpoints and deployment services), the data/AI layer (feature engineering, training, evaluation, NLP and classification), and the infrastructure layer (containers, model versioning, automated workflows and production deployment).
bullets: Moved models out of notebooks into containerized inference endpoints with versioning and rollback, giving the team its first repeatable path to production.
Developed NLP and classification models over client text and transactional data, owning feature engineering through offline evaluation.
Automated the training and evaluation loop, taking idea-to-measured-result from 9 days to under 2 and making weekly iteration realistic for a 4-person team.
Introduced experiment tracking and model versioning, replacing the filename-and-spreadsheet convention the team had been relying on.

projects.description: Underwriting and pricing analytics is how an insurer decides who to cover and at what price, backed by data rather than intuition. Policy, claims, and customer records land in a warehouse through scheduled data pipelines; statistical and machine-learning models score risk on that data; and the results surface as dashboards and reports the underwriting and business teams actually read when setting rates or reviewing an applicant. It touches the front end (the dashboards and reports business stakeholders use), the back end (the ETL jobs and cloud data infrastructure that keep those numbers current), and the data side (the exploratory analysis and the risk and pricing models themselves).
bullets: Built statistical and machine learning models to support insurance underwriting and pricing decisions, moving risk assessment from rules-of-thumb toward data-driven scoring.
Developed gradient-boosted and generalized linear models over policy and claims history, improving risk-tier separation against the incumbent rules-based approach.
Performed exploratory data analysis on large policy and claims datasets to identify trends, segment behavior, and surface growth opportunities for the business.
Created dashboards and reports in Power BI and SQL to communicate model outputs to business stakeholders, giving underwriting and actuarial teams one shared view of model behavior.
Supported data pipeline development and ETL processes for analytics and reporting, consolidating policy, claims, and customer sources into a single analytics schema.
Added automated data-quality checks to ETL loads so malformed records were quarantined and flagged instead of silently skewing downstream model inputs.
Assisted senior engineers in building data infrastructure on cloud platforms, moving recurring analytical workloads off manual extracts onto scheduled pipelines.
Documented model assumptions, feature definitions, and validation results to support internal review of pricing and underwriting decisions.
